followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified task with clear completion criteria: synthesize evidence from given sources into a single, focused paragraph answering two specific historical questions, with an explicit instruction to be concise ("Don't ramble").

A few factors drove the choice:

1. **Task type fit:** This is fundamentally a constrained summarization/extraction task — pulling evidence from provided sources and reformatting it into a tight, defined output. That falls squarely in Plover's strongest territory (its top-rated tasks are well-specified extraction and reformatting requests with clear completion criteria), and it scores comparably on the relevant internal evals.

2. **Benchmarks are effectively tied or favor Plover:** On the eval categories that matter here (Summarization, Extraction & Retrieval), the two models are within run-to-run variance of each other. Plover also edges ahead on IFEval-adjacent strictness in following the format constraint (one paragraph, no rambling) — though both are strong there.

3. **Preference alignment with no quality cost:** The task has low latitude (clear structure, specific questions, source-bound). Plover self-reports preferring exactly this kind of low-latitude, well-defined work. Since preferences don't affect output quality per the documentation, this is essentially a tiebreaker that points toward Plover anyway.

There was no harm-adjacent or warmth-sensitive element that would have favored Willet, so nothing pulled the other direction.
